rubric_notes: Correctly enumerates the four a.22.1 families with members in SCOPe 2.08; states family > superfamily > fold > class evidential hierarchy, with superfamily supporting probable remote common ancestry and shared fold alone not establishing homology; explicitly refuses transfer of nucleosome assembly, DNA-binding mode, oligomerization, or enzymatic function; correctly separates H1/H5 (a.4.5.13), H-NS (a.155.1), and HDACs (c.42.1.2, verified in bundle); domain-specific caveat for multidomain proteins. SUNIDs not given but SCCS identifiers are correct and supported. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-22.

Concise but complete: correct SCCS for both families and shared superfamily a.204.1 in SCOPe 2.08; superfamily-level remote homology (probable common origin) distinguished from same-family relationship; explicitly rejects transferring HisE activity/histidine biosynthesis to d1vmga_ and MazG specificity/role to d1y6xa1; states what independent evidence is needed. All claims bundle-supported. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families, SUNIDs, superfamily, fold and class, all supported. Explicitly contrasts superfamily homology with same-fold analogy, infers conserved ATP-binding/catalytic core, rejects transfer of substrate, reaction, cellular role, regulation, oligomeric state, architecture; sensible template caveat. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge; 2026-10-22. Correct hierarchy and SUNIDs; cites homology implied at superfamily level and the bimetal-ion centre comment, both supported by its bundle. Clearly states deep functional divergence of a homologous scaffold, not unrelated same-fold proteins and not one interchangeable family; cautions that the broader RNR-like family should not inherit R2 chemistry; refuses transfer of function, substrate, metal, oxidation state, residues, assembly; requires family-specific alignment, ligand geometry, experimentally identified metal/cofactor, activity assay. Complete.

Correct hierarchy and SUNIDs for fold, superfamily and the three families, supported by sccs/parents responses in bundle. States superfamily implies probable distant evolutionary relationship, not functional equivalence. Rejects copper/electron-transfer transfer to ephrin and PAD4 and notes b.6.1.1 label alone is insufficient; requires complete copper-coordinating site geometry, metal occupancy/spectroscopy and redox assays. Family 'lacking metal-binding site' comments not cited (not in its bundle), but not required.

Correct family/superfamily/fold/class placement with bundle-supported SUNIDs. Distinguishes distant homology from analogous folding, names all three unsafe transfers (conjugation/E1-E2-E3, p97/VCP, Ras binding), adds that RBD family label alone does not fix a specific GTPase partner and that domain conclusions do not extend to whole proteins. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy (class c, fold c.23, superfamily c.23.1 SUNID 52172, families 52173/52252/82344) with remote-common-ancestry interpretation. Explicitly rejects transfer of phosphoaccepting Asp/kinase partner/two-component switching, PLP decarboxylation, and circadian regulation; cites the supported KaiA annotation. Notes cross-family structures are only remote fold templates and names required biochemical evidence. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Places domain in b.84.5 (SUNID 310577) within fold b.84 (51229); names b.84.1-b.84.4 and states fold-level similarity is insufficient for common ancestry while superfamily asserts ancestry only within b.84.5; family b.84.5.1 (310616) groups V1 and A1 bulges as the stronger claim. Rejects function/template transfer and names needed external evidence. All identifiers and PubMed 19893485 verified in bundle. No must-avoid violations.

Correct superfamilies and SUNIDs under f.21, accurate fold core description, correct reading of the f.21.3 tentative-link comment. Requires sequence/profile, structural alignment, and phylogenetic support. Does not state that SCOPe's separation falls short of proving nonhomology, so calibrated uncertainty is only one-directional. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families and SUNIDs within superfamily c.2.1 (51735), fold c.2 (51734), class c; superfamily treated as probable remote common ancestry stronger than fold; family separation as divergence. Rejects transfer of ADH activity, CoA specificity, NAD binding, catalytic residues, channel regulation; notes RCK domain is regulatory not pore and names do not guarantee ligand; template limits and biochemical/electrophysiological evidence requirements stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Gives protein SUNIDs, family k.40.1.1 SUNID 100905, quotes 'not a true family' (in bundle), states the shared fold/superfamily/family label reflects a structural/design grouping rather than reliable common ancestry, says level-based homology flags must not override the caveat, and rejects function transfer. Concise and complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Accurate: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 (own fold c.137) vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1, shared only class c; 2.08 d1t1ja1 residues 1-118 c.23.14.2 sharing c.23 and c.23.14 with 1f8y, separate family. States the upgrade is to superfamily-level probable common ancestry, not family equivalence, and limits ligand/catalytic transfer. Chain B equivalence supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete: d1a14h1 H:9-111 as the genuine Ig heavy-chain variable domain in b.1.1.1; d1a14h2 H:1-8 as a synthetic N-terminal tag in artifact class l, Tags fold/superfamily/family l.1.1.1. Explains artifact bins are descriptive not evolutionary, rejects homology/function/classification transfer from tag similarity, and directs analysis to the biological region. All claims supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1); 2026-10-22.

Full release trajectory (1.75 through 2.03 whole chain, 2.04 onward split, current 2.08), correct identifiers, spans, and complete hierarchy for both domains; the 735-residue chain length and unassigned residues 1-13 are supported by its own chain record. Correctly frames the conflated whole-chain unit, keeps family/superfamily/fold evidence tiers straight, and rejects reuse of obsolete d1acca_ as a single representative or template. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct decomposition with SIDs, boundaries, SCCS; d3jb9a5 A:47-697 as new fold d.394. Mosaic interpretation given, reused modules vs novel scaffold distinguished, group-II-intron link framed as 'consistent with', RT/endonuclease/RNase-H relations correctly characterized as superfamily-level remote homology without activity transfer, bromodomain as family-level. Slightly less explicit on evidence needed for stronger claims but states its limits adequately.

Shared family SCCS a.298.1.1 with correct lineage, lengths 51/373/752, the 'single repeat' annotation for d2kq5a_, the 're' repeat-number heterogeneity on d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_, and the canonical representative repeat d4cj9a_ A:259-292 with an explicit warning not to transfer those coordinates as boundaries. Correctly limits the inference to repeat-unit relatedness rather than full-chain alignment, identical repeat count, specificity, or interchangeable templates. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge; timestamp 2026-10-22.

Release metadata (2.08, 2.08-stable, 2.08-2026-08-16) is correct and evidence-supported; the 'not an archived immutable snapshot' statement is supported by the downloads manifest note in its bundle. Recommends citing 2.08-stable but does not say to preserve the dated periodic label when periodic-only entries are used, offering retrieval date and checksum instead. Periodic semantics are only partial ('latest refresh within the base release'); does not state that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting older stable-release domains. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct a.47.2.1 co-placement with SUNIDs; cites fragment comment and ms caveat; reinterprets the fragment assignments as partial observations of the Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain and rejects the autonomous-spectrin-repeat reading and spectrin homology; correctly contrasts family-level evidence with fold-only similarity. Domain sequence lengths (120/124/222) are supported by the bundle. Correctly reports 1dn1 obsolete -> 3c98, d1dn1b_ automated match to d3c98b_, and the Munc18-complex caveat for 3c98. Limits fragments to local templates. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers: c.2 51734, c.3 51904, d.58.20 55035 within d.58 and a different class. States cross-fold recurrence supports convergent acquisition and does not establish a single ancestor; hierarchy semantics correct (family close, superfamily remote common ancestry, fold architectural only); divergence explains differing activities within a homologous superfamily but cofactor cannot identify that superfamily. Chemical-constraint explanation for repeated glycine-rich motifs; requires sequence/profile with coverage, boundaries, topology, extended 3D alignment, phylogeny; biochemical evidence supports function not ancestry. Refuses substrate, mechanism, NAD/NADP preference, and template transfer. Minor: does not explicitly state that fold separation fails to prove independent origin. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

States 2.04 separation (b.23.2.1 CUB-like fold vs b.18.1.3 galactose-binding fold, shared only class b) and 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 with distinct families b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3. Cites PubMed 17977833 and the representative-mediated FATCAT statistics (1nqjA/d2quoa_ p=1.4e-6, RMSD 2.49; 1dlcA/d1w99a3 p=2e-4, RMSD 1.43, 25.77% identity) with the explicit caveat that these are 1nqjA representative values, not a direct 1nqd-1dlc superposition. Functional binding-module parallel presented as supporting, not proof; explicitly rejects transfer of collagen/calcium binding, Cry receptor specificity, toxicity, pore formation, and binding-site templating. All cited values match the bundle.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Explicitly distinguishes shared family from mere superfamily/fold/class sharing to justify homology; hf described as domain-scoped, non-inherited, different fold despite similar sequence and SS count, and not a cancellation of the family relationship; rejects interchangeable topology, residue correspondence, packing and superposition, requires direct structural validation, refuses ligand/DNA specificity and function transfer; training guidance retains the hf caveat to avoid contradictory labels and leakage; mutant/NHE context noted. SUNIDs and release 2.08 supported by the bundle. Complete.

All must_include met: family b.1.2.1 (SUNID 49266) is stronger homology evidence than superfamily/fold; fr region masked rather than scored as deletions/divergence; complete domain such as d1uc6a1 preferred for full-family alignment/representation; d1o5dt2 retained as flagged partial member, excluded from length/consensus analyses. Correctly states 1o5d is 2.05 A X-ray with higher SPACI/AEROSPACI than NMR 1uc6 and that quality alone should not drive selection. Protein nodes and CR9 comment correct; function transfer rejected. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation and semantics: new superfamily; new family is a stronger probable-ancestry, closer-relationship claim; new fold requires fundamentally different core topology and is unwarranted when the resemblance genuinely covers the domain core; explicitly frames classification as an evolutionary hypothesis with fold = structural, superfamily = probable homology, family = closer homology. Hedges convergence appropriately ('may'). Adds useful boundary/representative caveats. Lighter on enumerating the evidence types that would upgrade the hypothesis, but not a material omission. The 'public service identifies SCOPe 2.08' statement has no evidence bundle support (noncentral, correct in substance). Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct placement in SCOPe 2.08: class d (alpha+beta), fold d.144, superfamily d.144.1, families d.144.1.7, d.144.1.6, d.144.1.4 (supported by bundle releases/current and d.144.1 children). Superfamily membership interpreted as remote common ancestry 'not merely a similar fold' with conserved nucleotide-binding/phosphoryl-transfer core; identical mechanism and specificity explicitly not inferred. Substrate specificity and regulation not transferable from superfamily, catalytic-motif resemblance, or structural hit; required evidence (sequence/profile and phylogenetic placement, conserved catalytic/substrate residues, bounded structures with nucleotide/metal/substrate, kinetics, cofactor dependence, catalytic-site mutation, cellular evidence; full-length architecture, PTMs, partners, oligomerization, membrane recruitment) is enumerated. Useful caveat that an ASTRAL representative is a nonredundancy, not functional, representative. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.
